entries.name: Standing low roundhouse shadow kick
entries.sourceDose: 3 × 2 per kicking leg = 12 attempts, 6/leg. From the same short fighting stance with the kicking leg initially at the rear, turn the support foot with the pelvis, lift and sweep the bent thigh, then extend only through a controllable low arc, recoil and return to the starting stance; hold 2 s. Foot stays below hip height. Rest 20 s between the two reps, 60 s between legs, 90 s between rounds, and 90 s after the final round.

Foot stays below hip height. Rest **20 s between the two reps**, **60 s between legs**, **90 s between rounds**, and **90 s after the final round**. | Integrate stance-leg rotation with free-leg acceleration and recovery. Accelerate the hip/thigh briskly; keep a soft knee at extension and brake the leg actively. No target, impact, partner contact, head-height kick, jump or spinning kick. explosive_progression_note: Two-Hand Landmine Bent-Over Row — fast pull from a pause moves the observation to rapid traction from a settled load; Kettlebell Swing — dead-stop two-hand repetitions supplies deliberate hip acceleration from a parked bell. This separates trunk-still arm force from hip-driven force, while Plyo Push-Up — hands elevated introduces a small hand-receiving dose and the lower rotation slot introduces a low actively recoiled kick. Compared with Class 1, prescribed ball releases change from 13 to 7, bilateral foot-landing events change from 6 to 0, bilateral hand-receiving events change from 0 to 3. With actual recovery reviewed, require a steady row hinge, a controlled bell park and soft hand reception before another effort. If the landmine load or grip is unsuitable, use the listed seated bilateral band row with its settled start for remaining row attempts; if hand reception is unqualified, use the listed nonflight incline push-up for remaining E3 work and log zero hand receptions.
